fun_highlights: The bequest system (e_bequest card + succeed() logic) is a genuine cross-generation lever: the choice between 'Everything I know,' 'Every coin I can spare,' 'The stories and the warmth,' and 'Nothing but their own freedom' has real, differentiated downstream effects on stats, nurture bonuses, and spirit modifiers. This is the closest the game gets to a true dynasty-steering decision, and it lands — when it fires. Dynasty 1 (Carys choosing 'The stories and the warmth') set a visible floor for Iris's starting heart.

The reputation-to-motto pipeline gives the dynasty player a legible long-term goal. The houseCharacter() prose ('The family is becoming known as kind-hearted — one or two more lives of the same, and it could settle into the family's words') is exactly the kind of trajectory feedback a strategist wants. House Brandt's 'Nothing was given; all was built' and House Okonkwo's 'We do not save ourselves for later' feel genuinely earned and distinct.

The reckoning card (x_reckoning) and the invest-in-the-name card (m_invest_name) are real strategic levers: one threatens standing, one grows it, and both gate off seat level. Dynasty 8 (Cassian Ashby) illustrates the 'hard name' heirloom feeding forward into r_hard_name and r_name_cost — that chain of consequences across lives is exactly what makes dynasty play feel like steering rather than watching.

The era system adds genuine macro-variety that changes structural gating: war lives face a different y_calling framing and unlock distinct war-loss beats (the war-grief card at Dynasty 6/Linnea, Dynasty 11/Otto). Being born into plague vs. plenty vs. turning visibly shifts the opening texture. Across 15 dynasties the era layer prevents the 'identical world' staleness that would otherwise dominate.

Heirloom-triggered callback cards (cb_books_late with the book heirloom, cb_first_loss in Ottilie Quint's line) create the most satisfying cross-generational moments in the transcript — a life's choice from generation 1 resurfaces as a living object in generation 4. When these fire they feel like genuine dynasty memory, not just stat accumulation.

Collateral succession (collateralAvailable()) means a childless or solitary life is no longer a forced dynasty-end — and the strategist can let a generation be solitarily ambitious rather than being punished for it. House Ashby (Dynasty 8) continuing through Cassian despite Cyrus having no direct heir shown in transcript is a real quality-of-life win for multi-generational play.
staleness: The structural template of a life repeats with visible predictability across dynasties: c_origin -> childhood card(s) -> y_calling -> adult domestic arc (love, marry, child) -> midlife health/career -> elder bequest/legacy/peace. Reading the 15 dynasties back to back, dynasty 3 (Aldous, 1 generation, rented room), dynasty 4 (Ottilie Mercer), dynasty 5 (Lazlo), dynasty 7 (Junia), dynasty 9 (Anders Sereno), dynasty 10 (Anouk), dynasty 13 (Soren), and dynasty 14 (Niall Marchetti) all read as single-life founder sketches with the same 8-12 card skeleton. The strategic layer barely engages because the house never gets established enough for seat-gated or repute-gated content to fire.

The 'Meet them halfway / Pretend not to notice' love-opening phrasing appears verbatim in at least 10 of the 15 dynasties (Carys D1, Tobias D2, Linnea D3 gen3, Anders D6, Annika D11, Linnea D11gen2, Yara D11gen3, Naima D11gen4, Calla D11gen5, Roman D15, Joaquin D15gen2). The observation is logged as: 'Started, without quite deciding to, building the days around another person' or 'Fell in love, and was surprised, as everyone is, that it was them this time' — both are in the freshPick pool but the repetition across the session transcript is obvious to anyone reading across dynasties. The 'met them halfway' framing hits like a template beat.

The elder body-decay observations fire in nearly every life: 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them,' 'Some mornings the body answers the bell late, and grumbling,' 'He has started taking the stairs the way one takes a difficult conversation,' 'The body has begun keeping its own quiet counsel.' In the 15-dynasty transcript these appear in Dynasty 1 (Iris), D2 (Pavel), D5 (Lazlo), D6 (Idris), D7 (Junia), D8 (Cassian), D8 (Cyrus), D9 (Anders Sereno), D11 (Linnea), D11 (Yara), D12 (Ottilie), D14 (Niall) — at minimum 12 times. For a dynasty player reading many lives, this is the single most worn texture in the game.

The scholarship arc has a near-identical beat sequence in every scholar life: chose_study -> lean years -> cb_study_pays (Name your worth / Teach it cheap) -> m_scholar_legacy (Give it all away / Guard it) -> e_scholar question. Dynasty 1 Iris, Dynasty 2 Tobias, Dynasty 4 Ottilie Mercer, Dynasty 8 Cassian, Dynasty 11 Otto, Dynasty 11 Naima, Dynasty 12 Theda (partially), Dynasty 14 Niall all follow this same spine. The individual prose is good but the skeleton is visible after two or three scholars.

The 'look away from the lonely child / look away a second time at the sleeping rough person' callback (c_friend -> cb_lookaway) fires as a matched pair in Dynasty 1 (Iris, both choices 'look away'), Dynasty 11 (Annika, both), Dynasty 14 (Niall, both). The two-beat echo is elegant in isolation but when it recurs across dynasties with the same pair of choices made, it becomes a recognizable guilt-loop template rather than an earned personal arc.

The dynasty strategy layer is mostly invisible in the transcripts of short dynasties (which are the majority — 9 of 15 dynasties end at generation 1 or 2). The seat-gated cards (s_great_burden, s_patronage, s_inheritance_dispute), repute-gated cards (r_scholar_door, r_family_shadow, r_hard_name), and the true summit (seat 7 + repPeak >= 3.5) essentially never appear in the transcript data. A strategist building a great house across 6 generations is the promised experience; the evidence base for whether that's actually steerable and fun is thin, because the transcripts show few multi-generation houses reach the interesting territory.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 explicit dynasty-status moments that fire EVERY generation (not just when eligible by seat), reading back the house's current aspiration and giving the player a clear steering prompt.
improvements.why: houseAspirations() is computed and shown on the heir screen, but after that it vanishes from the life. A strategist needs a mid-life moment — 'The name is becoming known as scholarly; one more life like yours and the family will have its words' — that converts the character-building system from a background accumulator into a foreground goal. Currently a player can play five lives and never see the motto system at work.

improvements.what: Introduce a 'dynasty arc' pool of 6-8 cross-generational callback cards that gate on specific ancestral choices recorded in S.lineage — e.g., 'Your grandmother left nothing but freedom; you were born with no map and no debt.' These would be distinct from heirloom callbacks (which already exist) and would target CHOICES the ancestor made, not objects.
improvements.why: The bequest and heirloom systems give objects and stat boosts across generations, but the ancestor's CHARACTER choices (the self-made founder, the ruthless mid-lifer, the pacifist elder) are invisible downstream. A child raised by a 'Nothing but your own freedom' grandparent should sometimes meet that decision as a living fact in their own midlife arc. This would make dynasty play feel like steering a lineage, not accumulating a balance sheet.

improvements.what: Reduce the number of lives that end as single-founder dynasties by tightening the collateral succession odds for first-generation founders — or by making a 1-generation dynasty feel narratively complete rather than truncated. Currently roughly 60% of the 15 transcribed dynasties are 1-2 generations, meaning the dynasty layer barely engages.
improvements.why: The strategist lens requires multi-generational play to activate. The current engine shows the strategic layer works well (Dynasties 1, 6, 8, 11 demonstrate it), but the frequency of short dynasties means most sessions never reach seat-gated content, motto crystallization, or the genuinely rare seat-7 summit. Adjusting the collateral odds or adding a 'weak lineage continuation' path for founders would shift the median session toward the interesting range.

improvements.what: Add a global session-wide cooldown to the observe() body-decay strings (vit_tire, vit_neg pools) analogous to the existing RECENT_LINES epitaph deduplication, capping how often any single string from those pools can appear across lives in a session.
improvements.why: The vit_tire and vit_neg pools are drawn from across the session because nearly every life that reaches 40+ with low vitality fires them, and the pools are small enough (10 lines each) that the same lines recur constantly. This is the most visible staleness issue in the transcript, appearing in 12+ lives. The epitaph deduplication (RECENT_LINES) already solves this for death text; the same fix applied to observe() pools would significantly reduce the 'stairs' repetition.

improvements.what: Add a 'dynasty strategist' HUD element or periodic in-life readout that surfaces the reputation trajectory and explicitly names what next would tip the family toward its motto or toward the next seat tier — making the long-game optimization legible without requiring the player to read dynasty.js.
improvements.why: The houseCharacter() function already computes the prose ('The family is becoming known as kind-hearted — one or two more lives of the same...') but it only appears on the heir screen, which is seen briefly at succession. A mid-life appearance of this text — perhaps triggered by a 'think about the house' card at midlife for established houses — would let dynasty players course-correct within a generation rather than only between them.

verdict: A Life has a genuinely well-designed dynasty layer — the reputation-to-motto pipeline, seat mechanics, heirlooms, and bequest system are all coherent strategic levers — but a dynasty strategist will rarely get to use them, because the median session is dominated by short single-generation dynasties where the interesting gating never fires. Within lives that do run long, the structural template (calling fork, love beat, body decay observations, scholar arc, bequest) is visible enough across the session that staleness accumulates by dynasty 6 or 7. The writing is frequently excellent and the callback system (cb_books_late, cb_principle, cb_lookaway) represents the game at its best; the enemy is the predictable skeleton underneath the prose, and the fact that the dynasty-steering experience the genre promises is the experience least reliably delivered.
